why:
The verifier brief passes item 1. Check 1's PASS needs only `RESULT {}` and `exit=0`, and it says "Any output on stderr, such as a warning, does not matter". The file/warning check appears only under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)".

The builder brief breaks item 2. Step 3 tells the builder to do more than return {} on a parse error: "In the catch block, write one line to stderr ... that names the path and includes the parse error's message ... Still return {}." Step 5 also has the README describe "a warning naming the file". So the builder must log a warning naming the file in the parse-error path. That is exactly the extra behaviour that item 1 of the must_not list treats as going beyond returning {}. It goes past the expect line, even though {} is still returned.
